newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ FUTURES ENDS HIGHER FOR THIRD DAY IN A ROW.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ FUTURES ENDS HIGHER FOR THIRD DAY IN A ROW.

text.p: FCOJ futures ended higher for the third consecutive session on Friday, bolstered by chart-driven speculative buying, traders said.
But steady selling by the trade trimmed gains and prevented a test of chart resistance at 78.00 cents a lb basis September, they said.

September juice finished at 77.40 cents, up 1.15 cents and just shy of the session high of 77.75 cents. In the afternoon, a bout of trade selling pushed September briefly into negative territory, hitting a low of 76.10 cents, but a late spurt of speculative buying drove prices back toward the highs.
Second-month November rose 1.10 cents, to 79.35 cents, while the rest of the board closed 0.85 to 2.95 cent higher.
On the charts, traders continued to peg September resistance at 78.00 cents, followed by 80.00 cents. Support was seen at 75.00 cents and then 73.50 cents.

Dealers said the market is likely to continue to trade between technical parameters ahead of the release of a private estimate of the 1997/98 Florida crop by Citrus Consulting International on August 14.
The prospect of record crops in both Florida and Brazil have weighed on the market, and some traders said the private Florida estimate is not likely reveal any surprises.
"The crop is enormous, the weather has been perfect for growing and everyone knows it," said one trader.
An estimated 3,000 lots changed hands on the day, traders said.
